moves.headline: Intuit falls 13% after results as lowered guidance tied to the Mailchimp sale meets a weak market
moves.summary: Intuit shares fell 12.8% to $270.44 the day after it reported first-quarter results that beat forecasts but announced the sale of Mailchimp and adjusted its revenue guidance. The decline was amplified by the broad technology sell-off on November 20.
why: Intuit reported first-quarter revenue up 12% to $4.4 billion and adjusted EPS of $2.91, about 10% above the consensus, and said results were above the top of its guidance. In the same release it announced an agreement to sell Mailchimp, the email-marketing business it bought for about $12 billion in 2021, to Bending Spoons, and made corresponding adjustments to its Consumer segment and total company revenue guidance, while keeping its operating income and EPS guidance.

Investors read the Mailchimp sale as an admission that the acquisition did not work, and the lower revenue outlook as a sign of slower growth in the remaining businesses. The reaction came on a day when software and other technology stocks were sold heavily alongside semiconductors.
context: On November 20 the Nasdaq Composite fell 5.3% and the S&P 500 3.7%, pushing the S&P 500 and the Dow into correction territory and wiping out the Nasdaq’s gain for 2026. Semiconductors led the fall, capping their worst week since 2001.

src.title: Dow, S&P 500 enter correction as Nasdaq plunges in AI stock sell-off (UPI)
